source_findings.finding: Semantic disk-hit path invokes finish_typed then returns before FunctionStore creation/restore/save at 946-1009. Rows with only types:reused,analyze:reused,verify:executed take this path. New encoder and group lock are not invoked on that successful no-op path; FunctionSession checkpoint adds only one extra group Arc clone/drop.

Keys, scalar filters, replay and rebasing are unchanged. Reuse still deep-clones the actual TypedFunction for current rebasing; successful reuse retains the same Arc<Entry> and owner. Publication removes its old all-CFG temporary clone. Warm encoded fragments read OnceLock without group mutex; group lock occurs only attempted first retention and final owner drop. No selector invalidation or all-function rewrap on successful hits found.

Real extra costs: one nested owner allocation per newly saved function, Arc indirection, retained byte copy per first admitted fragment, exact Limits comparison per cached fragment, and mutex on admission/final drop. These can trade memory and cold work for saved warm serialization; local byte-oracle tests do not establish end-to-end net benefit.

Default max_source_bytes=16MiB. Both retained FunctionStore files are 5,314,392 bytes, so a full current+checkpoint pair at this fixture is below the cap. No evidence that cap pressure explains these measurements. More live failed/externally cloned snapshots or other fixtures can cause fallback; full cap causes repeated ordinary encoding, not semantic invalidation.
